name: How to Prepare for Your Vanity and Cabinet Installation

step.name: Step 1: Measure Accurately. Before you even order your vanity or cabinets, take precise measurements of the space. Measure the wall width, floor space, and consider the clearances around the toilet and any door swings. Don’t forget to measure the height from the floor to any windowsills or light switches. Accurate measurements prevent issues with fit and accessibility later on.

Accurate measurements prevent issues with fit and accessibility later on.

step.name: Step 2: Confirm Plumbing and Electrical Locations. Take note of where your existing water supply lines and drain are. If you’re using a pre-fabricated vanity, check if these align with its design. If not, be prepared for potential plumbing adjustments. Similarly, mark the locations of any electrical outlets or light switches that might be affected by the new cabinet placement. This helps your installer anticipate any necessary modifications.

step.name: Step 3: Clear the Area. On the day of installation, make sure the bathroom is clear of any obstacles. Remove toiletries, towels, and anything else from the old vanity or cabinet. Move any small rugs, wastebaskets, or decor out of the way to give the installers plenty of room to work safely and efficiently. This simple step can save time and prevent accidental damage.

step.name: Step 4: Inspect Your New Vanity/Cabinets. When your new items arrive, give them a thorough inspection before installation begins. Check for any damage from shipping, ensure all parts are present, and verify that the dimensions match what you ordered. It's much easier to address any issues before the installation process starts rather than midway through.

step.name: Step 5: Protect Your Space. While installers will take precautions, it's a good idea to lay down drop cloths or old blankets to protect your flooring, especially if it's new. Cover nearby furniture if dust is a concern. This small effort can help keep your home cleaner and protect your investment.

step.name: Step 6: Prepare the Walls. If you're replacing an old vanity, ensure the wall behind it is clean, dry, and structurally sound. Patch any holes or imperfections and make sure it's ready to accept the new installation. If the wall is uneven, your installer might need to make adjustments to ensure the vanity is level and securely fastened.
step.text: What to Prepare Before You Start Beyond the physical preparations, consider the overall look you're aiming for. Have any complementary items like mirrors, lighting, or new faucets ready if they're part of the installation plan. Thinking through these details beforehand helps the installation team, like Frasheski Construction, execute your vision seamlessly. If you’re unsure about fitting larger items, measuring only at floor level is a common mistake; remember to account for baseboards, trim, and wall irregularities.
